plan.name: Resolve and stage existing Python applications
plan.summary: Admit Python existing-code manifests and resolve one unambiguous enclosing application from their named source selections, with or without root requirements.txt; use application-relative component scopes, references and input paths only for this new mode, preserving legacy Python and TypeScript rules and Python lexical identities and exact contract bytes. Add the application context and staging APIs specified by the acceptance tests: preserve the application layout and original bytes in a separate workspace, include the verification project, tests, sibling code and resources, reject ambiguous roots, missing inputs, escapes and symlinks, and bind canonical inventory provenance to every staged file. Select the workspace's dependency image through the existing PythonDepsImage API using the staged application root and recursive requirements inputs, retaining its validation, isolation, immutable-image and standard-library behavior without another installer. Keep existing-Python code execution unsupported, including manifests without explicit components, and preserve the explicit-component guard and model-only path until the next issue supplies the execution adapter. Update SPEC.md and README with the available foundation, path bases, staging and provenance rules and execution limitation under D-0122, citing D-0054, D-0158, D-0168, D-0177 and D-0178 as applicable and this ratified plan; the merger must record the Python existing-code and application-context identity policy extension using decision tooling, and complete unavailable Docker/network validation as Merger work without editing decisions or ratified statements and locks in this build.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationContextAndSelections
tests.says: An ordinary nested Python application loads from its separate verification directory, resolves application-relative selections and exact Python identities without importing code, and retains project-relative model and manifest driver paths.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationRejectsInvalidContexts
tests.says: After accepting a valid application, discovery and staging reject ambiguous roots, missing selections and inputs, invalid path bases, and linked sources, resources and verification directories.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationStagingAndProvenance
tests.says: Staging preserves all application bytes and package layout, binds every staged file to provenance, and yields stable identities and fingerprints across relocation while sibling, source, resource, test and driver changes affect fingerprints.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationDependencyRoot
tests.says: Dependency selection uses staged application requirements and recursive inputs, preserves immutable-image and artifact evidence on reuse, and never substitutes verification-directory dependencies or later changes to original files.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationDependencyFailuresAndStandardLibrary
tests.says: The no-requirements path needs no Docker, and missing, escaping, cyclic, linked or unsupported application requirements fail without a fallback image.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationPreservesLegacyAndRefusesExecution
tests.says: New application discovery leaves legacy Python identity and TypeScript package discovery and staging intact; declarations still cannot run code verification or yield evidence.
